THREE STEPS, IN THIS ORDER - REPORT, ASK TO INSPECT, THEN RULE. (1) REPORT every finding below to the CB in plain words: what the test pins, and which other correct implementation it would reject. Never paste an id as if it explained itself. (2) ASK THE CB WHETHER TO INSPECT, and WAIT for the answer. Do not investigate unasked and do not rule unasked - this check reads test source only, so every finding here is a QUESTION, and the CB decides whether it is worth your time to chase. Asking them to adjudicate it themselves is the other failure: they should be choosing whether you dig, not doing the digging. (3) IF THEY SAY YES, inspect with TEST_FITNESS.md - read the test BODY rather than the diff (the diff hides the helpers) to see whether a symbol is asserted BY NAME or discovered by behaviour; grep the BASE tree to check the "the golden fix introduces this" claim, the single most common false finding here; open the posters; and MEASURE where the read runs out. What the evidence then shows to be a FALSE POSITIVE you clear YOURSELF, with that evidence as the reason - it is recorded and replays on every later audit, so the gate stays green without anyone re-typing anything. What the evidence shows to be REAL you report as a defect to fix, not something to clear. Where it stays inconclusive, say so and go back to the CB. NEVER clear one you have not inspected: that turns a blocker into a formality and the CB never learns their tests were questioned. HOW THIS DIMENSION WORKS. Every overfit finding above BLOCKS - no QC pass is recorded, so oracle and nop stay grounded until each one is ruled on. But each is a heuristic read off test source, not a proven defect: this check cannot see the REPOSITORY, where the rubric's "plausible implementation has precedent in the repo" is decided, nor the POSTERS, where a literal that looks golden-only is often the spec. So each is a QUESTION, answered in either direction with a mandatory reason: `--adjudicated <id>=cleared:"why"` drops it to OK, `=confirmed:"why"` promotes it to a real defect to fix. DO NOT loosen an assertion merely because it is listed - on a well-built task most of these clear, and weakening a good test is the more expensive mistake. TEST_FITNESS.md is not reserved for a contested ruling - it is how you FORM one: the investigation: the digest, both posters, and a container where the alternative implementation can be RUN in about two seconds, which settles it as evidence instead of opinion. UNDERFIT - a plausible wrong fix that still scores - is not reachable here at all and needs that same procedure.

READ instruction.md WITH THE IMAGES SET ASIDE and decide: could a competent engineer locate and fix this defect from the prose alone? Report the answer to the CB as a WARNING either way - this is never a blocker. LEAN: UNCLEAR - the signals point both ways. Read it and decide.

findings.title: instruction.md uses 4 word(s) that also appear in the golden fix's changed lines. The playbook cuts "words that point at the cause" ("its radius is wrong"). If a word names the ELEMENT (the thing that looks wrong), keep it - the playbook wants the element named. If it names the CAUSE or mechanism, cut it. ADVISORY - never a blocker.

instruction.md has 2 sentence(s) where the symptom is unspecific: a general phrase stands alone, the affected element is never named by type, or the text never says what kind of problem it is nor points to where the correct result can be seen. The playbook's Dim 4 Fail ("Unspecific Symptoms") is e.g. "Something does not render correctly" with nothing after it. Name the element by type, and either give one plain word for the defect ("empty", "spiky", "missing") or point to the image that shows the correct result, without naming the cause. ADVISORY - never a blocker.
